title: I’m a 3D animator learning to make a game with AI. Here’s what I’ve made so far.
author: DoubtAdorable4514
selftext:
Hi, I’ve worked in 3D animation for about five years, mainly using Blender. I also used Unreal, but I didn’t know how to code. I’ve been working on this idea for over three months, with about a month and a half spent actually developing it in Unity with AI.



The game is called Catadel: Slot Defense. You spin to summon troops, trigger cascading combos, and defend your castle. The video is actual gameplay from the current build.



Since 3D is what I’m familiar with, I decided to mix 3D and 2D. I still find it difficult to rely entirely on AI for 3D work, but luckily I can fix and adjust things myself. That’s helped me keep going. I also use AI-generated artwork for backgrounds, item images, and the logo.



Getting the first version working was easier than I expected. The hard part came later. As the project got bigger, even small changes started taking lots of back-and-forth and eating up tokens. Sometimes I just want to change one thing and end up spending ages on it.



I’m still working on the demo. Has anyone else run into the same problem with small changes getting more expensive as the project grows? I’d like to hear how you handle it.



Would also love to hear what you think of the gameplay. Here’s the Steam page if you’d like to take a look. Wishlists are appreciated!



[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5147270/Catadel\_Slot\_Defense/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5147270/Catadel_Slot_Defense/)

comments.author: TallboyGames
comments.body:
Awesome work. This proves exactly what I believed to be the case after trying the AI assisted coding game dev journey since March of this year, and that is, people who will be successful at this, are the artists. Now that anyone can code, the true synergy shines when the person was already a talented artist. I found 3D animation to be my major bottleneck. If an asset pack didn't have the exact animation I needed, pretty much out of luck. The AI 3D generations also aren't perfect, not even close, so being able to fix them in blender is a key skill to have.

  
Keep it up, looks great!

replies.author: DoubtAdorable4514
replies.body: Thanks, that means a lot 😄 Being able to fix things in Blender has definitely helped, but I’m still learning a lot as I go. There’s plenty of trial and error behind what you see here haha. Hope your project is going well too!
